prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer stands above and behind a white salon washbasin (roughly 0.5–0.8 m below the camera), with a textured wall immediately to the right (0.3–0.6 m away) holding a mounted heater unit and a doorway and tiled floor further below and ahead (1.5–2.2 m away). A reclined person sits in a chair to the left of the basin with their blurred head resting in the basin's neck cutout about 0.5–0.7 m below the camera wearer, facing upward toward the ceiling and camera wearer with their clasped hands resting on their lap about 0.6 m below their head, while the camera wearer's gloved hands hold a foil packet within arm's reach (0.3–0.5 m from the camera) directly above the basin right of the person's head. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer turns and shifts slightly leftward so the reclined person's body enters view from the left edge, while the wearer's hands move from holding the packet with the right hand (frame 1) to grasping it with both hands (frames 2–4) and lowering the left hand toward the basin edge next to the person's head (frame 5). Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical layering between the camera wearer's foreground hands, the mid-ground head and basin rim, and the recessed floor and doorway behind the chair. However, the depth map is unreliable on the Gaussian-blurred face region—rendering it as a smooth, bulging oval dome in frames 2–4—and over-brightens the upper-right textured wall so it appears artificially closer than the foreground hands.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates foreground objects in the lower half of the scene—specifically the camera wearer's gloved hands and foil packet at the bottom right (0.3–0.5 m away), the reclined person's head at the bottom left/center (0.5–0.7 m away), and the white washbasin surrounding them (0.5–0.8 m away)—while leaving the walls, door, floor, and the reclined person's torso and legs unsegmented. In frame 1, it separates the person's head (partially cut off at the bottom-left edge) from the camera wearer's left hand, foil packet, and right hand, which are positioned within arm's reach just to the right and slightly above the head; in frames 2–5, as the camera shifts left to show the full basin, the wearer's hands partially occlude the lower-right basin rim and the person's head rests inside the left neck recess. While the masks help delineate the exact contour of the basin rim around the wearer's occluding hands in frames 2, 4, and 5 and track the head silhouette despite heavy RGB face blurring, the map is highly unreliable in both class labels and temporal consistency. It misclassifies the foil packet as a 'cell phone' (frame 1), the washbasin as a 'toilet' (frame 2) or 'bowl' (frames 4–5), and a dark slot on the upper-right wall heater as a 'knife' (frames 3–4). Furthermore, it completely misses the basin in frames 1 and 3, fails to segment the reclined person's body in the chair (roughly 1.0–1.5 m away on the left), and drops the person's head mask in frames 2 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map attempts to track skeletal keypoints for the reclined person positioned to the left of the washbasin (0.5–1.5 m below the camera wearer) and the camera wearer's hands in the lower-right foreground (0.3–0.5 m away), while the surrounding room remains black. Across the 5 frames, it detects keypoints only in frames 2, 3, and 5—placing yellow body segments near the reclined person's torso, shoulders, and clasped hands on their lap in frames 2 and 3, a magenta hand cluster on the person's clasped hands at the bottom-left of frame 2 (roughly 1.2 m from the camera wearer and within the seated person's own arm's reach), and a compact yellow cluster on the person's head in frame 5. In frame 2, that magenta hand skeleton helps pinpoint the exact location of the reclined person's crossed hands at the dark lower-left frame boundary where the black cape and dim lighting make them hard to see in RGB. However, the pose map is largely unreliable under this steep top-down viewpoint and heavy occlusion: it completely misses all bodies and hands in frames 1 and 4, fails to detect the camera wearer's prominent gloved hands manipulating the packet in the lower-right foreground across all 5 frames, and collapses the reclined person's skeleton into tangled, anatomically implausible polygons that do not reliably indicate their upward-facing orientation.
